partial_progress.details: Phases 1-10 fully completed and independently verified. Phase 11 (deploy, audit, document) executed its full audit sweep as specified, but the sweep's own zero-hits gate failed: it surfaced thirteen core SKILL.md files and six additional command-file write sites carrying their own inline hand-rolled specs/state.json writes, never decomposed into this plan's phases. This is a Scope Hypothesis miss in the plan's originating research report, not a defect in any completed phase. Converting the residual surface is realistically several more phases at the size and rigor of Phases 4-9 and should be scoped as a follow-up task. See the implementation summary's Follow-ups section for the full itemized list.

memory_candidates.content: Before treating a plan's Scope Hypothesis baseline as reliable enough to skip re-measuring at the FINAL audit phase, run the definition-of-done grep across the WHOLE source store (not just the files the plan names) as early as possible -- ideally during planning, not only at the last phase. A research report's inline-write-site count can be wrong by an order of magnitude (this task's baseline: 9 scripts + 2 command files; actual full-repo count: also 13 core SKILL.md files + 6 more command-file sites) when the report enumerated known hand-rolled jq/mv call sites via targeted greps rather than a single repo-wide pattern sweep. When an audit gate fails at the end of a plan, the correct response is to record the honest gap as a follow-up (with the specific file list) rather than either (a) silently expanding scope to convert everything found, which turns a bounded plan into an unbounded one mid-execution, or (b) silently declaring the phase complete despite the gate's own explicit non-negotiable wording ("any surviving hit is a phase failure, not an acceptable residual").

When a marker file must be readable by both a directly-invoked script (a skill/command's Bash tool call) and Claude Code hooks (Stop, UserPromptSubmit, etc.), and needs to be scoped per-session to avoid cross-session interference, key it by Claude Code's OWN native session UUID -- available as the $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID environment variable in every Bash tool invocation, and as the top-level .session_id field in every hook's stdin JSON. This is a DIFFERENT id space from an application-level session_id (e.g. this codebase's sess_{timestamp}_{hex} id, regenerated per command invocation), and is the only identifier both a plain script and every hook can independently resolve without one having to reconstruct it from the other via an indirect lookup.

When converting a family of scripts to route their writes through a new shared mutex-guarded helper, and several of those scripts have NO session_id parameter today (either never had one, or have dozens of pre-existing callers that pass none), add an optional --session-id flag that self-generates one (same portable pattern: sess_$(date +%s)_$(od -An -N3 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' ')) when omitted, rather than threading a required parameter through every existing caller. This keeps every existing call site working unchanged while still routing through the fail-closed mutex; attribution only improves where a caller opts in. Document this as a deliberate deviation, not a silent gap.
